l4_steps.name: Ingest ratified CBA language into rule repository
l4_steps.input: Ratified CBA document or amendment notice from union
l4_steps.output: Rule change requests logged in Jeppesen crew scheduling rule library
l4_steps.kpi: CBA rule ingestion initiated within 5 business days of ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual translation of legal CBA language into Jeppesen-readable scheduling constraints requires specialist knowledge; misinterpretation of trip rig, rest augmentation, or bidding period provisions is common

l4_steps.name: Configure duty/rest limits in scheduling engine
l4_steps.input: CBA duty/rest rule change requests; FAR Part 117 regulatory minimums
l4_steps.output: Updated Jeppesen rule set with CBA contractual duty time and rest limits
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of CBA rest rules coded and tested within 10 business days of ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 regulatory minimums and CBA contractual minimums differ by crew position (Captain vs F/O vs Flight Attendant); dual-layer rule stacking in Jeppesen increases configuration complexity and regression testing cycles

l4_steps.name: Configure premium pay triggers and trip rig rules
l4_steps.input: CBA pay schedule, premium pay provisions, trip rig and guarantee rules
l4_steps.output: Configured pay rules in SAP with all premium triggers (IROPS reassignment, hotel substitution, min-day guarantee)
l4_steps.kpi: Pay rule configuration accuracy ≥99.5%; zero retroactive pay adjustments attributable to misconfiguration in first post-implementation payroll cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA premium pay provisions (e.g., reassignment pay, deadhead premium, per diem differentials) are frequently misinterpreted; configuration errors are not detected until payroll run, creating retroactive liability

l4_steps.name: Validate rule configuration against CBA source text
l4_steps.input: Configured Jeppesen scheduling rules and SAP pay rules; original CBA text
l4_steps.output: Validation sign-off memo or change request list
l4_steps.kpi: Zero CBA violations attributable to misconfiguration within 90 days of new rule deployment
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated cross-reference tooling between CBA legal article numbers and Jeppesen rule IDs; validation is entirely manual and relies on individual analyst expertise, creating key-person dependency

l4_steps.name: Run pre-publication CBA compliance scan on draft schedule
l4_steps.input: Draft pairing solution from Jeppesen optimizer
l4_steps.output: Compliance report flagging CBA rule violations by article and step number
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance scan completed ≥2 hours before schedule publication deadline; scan must cover 100% of published pairings
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule changes driven by aircraft swaps or demand reforecast force rescan within 30-minute windows; Jeppesen batch compliance jobs may not complete in time, leaving residual violations undetected

l4_steps.name: Adjudicate violations and determine waiver or remediation
l4_steps.input: Compliance scan violation report
l4_steps.output: Decision per violation: remediate, obtain union waiver, or escalate
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of violations resolved or formally waived before schedule publication; adjudication cycle ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Some CBA violations require mutual union agreement for waiver (e.g., minimum rest reduction below contractual floor); union contact SLAs are not always met in real-time operations, creating publication holds

l4_steps.name: Remediate non-compliant pairings or assignments
l4_steps.input: List of violations requiring remediation; available crew pool and reserve positions
l4_steps.output: Revised compliant pairings or crew assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Remediation cycle ≤90 minutes; crew coverage maintained ≥97% post-remediation
l4_steps.pain_point: Remediation options are constrained by qualified reserve availability at domicile; fixing one CBA violation can cascade into secondary violations for adjacent pairings, triggering iterative rescan loops

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time crew duty times and rest windows
l4_steps.input: Live flight departure/arrival data; crew check-in and check-out events via ACARS
l4_steps.output: Real-time duty time dashboard; automated alerts for crews approaching CBA or FAR Part 117 limits
l4_steps.kpi: Duty limit alerts triggered ≥60 minutes before contractual limit; zero post-facto exceedances reported in monthly audit
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS data latency can delay duty-on/duty-off timestamp capture by 5–15 minutes, creating a window of undetected limit approach; iCrew alert thresholds must be manually calibrated per CBA article and crew category

l4_steps.name: Decide on duty extension or crew replacement during IROPS
l4_steps.input: Duty limit alert; flight delay status; qualified reserve availability at station
l4_steps.output: Documented decision: CBA extension invoked with crew consent, or replacement crew assigned
l4_steps.kpi: Crew replacement or extension decision made ≥45 minutes before departure; 100% of CBA waiver invocations logged with timestamp and crew consent reference
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA duty extensions require individual crew member consent; crew refusals during IROPS with no available replacement create cascading departure delays; iCrew has no automated consent-capture mechanism, exposing airline to grievance risk

l4_steps.name: Log and acknowledge crew grievance within CBA window
l4_steps.input: Written grievance submitted by crew member or union representative
l4_steps.output: Grievance case record with CBA article citation, incident timestamp, and acknowledgement sent to filer
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of grievances logged within 24 hours of receipt; formal acknowledgement delivered within CBA Step 1 filing window (typically 72 hours)
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA grievance filing windows (commonly 10–30 days from incident) require precise date/time stamping of the triggering event; SAP SuccessFactors case management is not purpose-built for CBA article-based aviation grievance workflows

l4_steps.name: Investigate grievance and retrieve corroborating data
l4_steps.input: Grievance case record; referenced duty period, flight, or pay event
l4_steps.output: Investigation dossier with duty logs, pay records, system-generated timestamps, and CBA article analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation completed within CBA Step 1 response window (typically 14 calendar days); 100% data retrieval from duty records for incidents ≤24 months old
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical duty and pay records span Jeppesen, iCrew, and SAP — three separate systems with no unified query interface; cross-system data extraction for grievance investigations is manual and can take 2–5 days, compressing response timelines

l4_steps.name: Assess grievance merit and issue management response
l4_steps.input: Investigation dossier; CBA articles cited in grievance
l4_steps.output: Merit assessment and formal Step 1 management response delivered to union
l4_steps.kpi: Management response delivered within CBA Step 1 deadline 100% of the time; grievance upheld rate ≤15%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent management responses across crew domiciles create arbitration precedents that constrain future positions; absence of a centralised CBA case law repository means analysts are unaware of prior rulings on identical fact patterns

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved grievance to arbitration
l4_steps.input: Grievance not resolved at Steps 1–3; arbitration demand notice from union
l4_steps.output: Arbitration brief, hearing schedule confirmed, award recorded in case management system
l4_steps.kpi: Arbitration win/settlement rate ≥60%; average cost per arbitration case ≤$15,000
l4_steps.pain_point: Arbitration preparation requires multi-year historical data retrieval; poor data quality from legacy crew system migrations (pre-2023) degrades management's evidentiary position and increases settlement risk

l4_steps.name: Execute monthly CBA compliance audit across all domiciles
l4_steps.input: Prior month's schedule execution data, payroll run outputs, duty logs from iCrew
l4_steps.output: Monthly compliance dashboard showing violation rate by CBA article, crew category, and domicile
l4_steps.kpi: Audit completed by day 5 of the following month; CBA violation rate ≤0.5% of all duty periods in scope
l4_steps.pain_point: ETL pipelines aggregating data from Jeppesen, iCrew, and SAP into Redshift are fragile; data latency or pipeline failures cause the audit to miss late-adjusted duties and produce understated violation counts

l4_steps.name: Distribute compliance report to union per CBA schedule
l4_steps.input: Monthly compliance dashboard from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Formatted union-facing compliance report delivered by CBA-stipulated deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered by 10th of the month 100% of the time; zero data discrepancies disputed by union within 30 days of delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA may require specific tabular formats or certified audit trail attachments not natively supported by Tableau; manual reformatting prior to union delivery introduces transcription errors and reputational risk

l4_steps.name: Determine if corrective action plan is required
l4_steps.input: Monthly compliance report; union objections or formal notices if any
l4_steps.output: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) initiated or formal closure memo issued
l4_steps.kpi: CAP initiated within 5 business days of audit finding confirmation; 100% of open CAPs closed within 60 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Systemic violations (e.g., recurring pay calculation errors, scheduling rule misapplication) require IT system changes with 4–8 week lead times; union may file class grievances covering the entire affected population while the CAP is open

l4_steps.name: Trigger CBA expiry alert and negotiation readiness review
l4_steps.input: CBA expiry date calendar alert (18-month advance trigger)
l4_steps.output: Negotiation readiness checklist; data extraction scope and timeline defined
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation preparation formally initiated ≥18 months before CBA expiry; zero missed expiry dates across all bargaining units
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple CBAs (pilots, flight attendants, dispatchers, ground operations) carry staggered expiry dates; tracking across contracts in SAP SuccessFactors requires custom calendar configuration that is not standard in the SuccessFactors Employee Central module

l4_steps.name: Extract historical compliance and cost data for bargaining
l4_steps.input: 3-year historical duty records, grievance case data, payroll actuals, IATA peer benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Bargaining data package: cost impact modelling of proposed rule changes, violation trend analysis, peer carrier benchmarks
l4_steps.kpi: Data package completed ≥12 months before CBA expiry; benchmark dataset covers ≥5 comparable peer carriers
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical data quality degrades beyond 24 months due to crew system migrations; IATA labour cost benchmarks are published on 12–18 month lag cycles, reducing relevance of peer comparisons at the bargaining table

l4_steps.name: Validate bargaining data package for negotiation
l4_steps.input: Draft bargaining data package from Labour Analytics
l4_steps.output: Approved bargaining data package or supplemental data extraction requests
l4_steps.kpi: Data package formally approved ≥10 months before CBA expiry; zero material data gaps surfaced at the bargaining table
l4_steps.pain_point: Union may dispute the airline's data methodology or system-of-record selection; absence of a jointly agreed data framework creates credibility risk and can stall early bargaining sessions

l4_steps.name: Implement ratified CBA rules in scheduling and pay systems
l4_steps.input: Ratified new or amended CBA document; confirmed effective date
l4_steps.output: Updated Jeppesen scheduling rules and SAP pay configuration; parallel-run test results; go-live sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: System implementation completed ≥14 calendar days before CBA effective date; zero pay errors attributable to new CBA rules in first post-implementation payroll cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA ratification often occurs within days of the contractual effective date, leaving insufficient time for Jeppesen rule testing cycles and SAP parallel pay run validation; compressed timelines increase risk of live-environment misconfiguration
